concepts.title: Structure and Functions of the Human Eye

questions.q: Name the main parts of the human eye.
questions.a: Cornea, iris, pupil, eye lens, ciliary muscles, retina and optic nerve.

questions.q: What is the function of the iris and pupil?
questions.a: The iris adjusts the pupil's size to control how much light enters the eye.

questions.q: Where is the image formed in the eye?
questions.a: On the retina, where light-sensitive cells turn it into electrical signals for the brain via the optic nerve.

concepts.title: Power of Accommodation and Limits of Vision

questions.q: What is power of accommodation?
questions.a: The eye lens's ability, by changing focal length through ciliary muscles, to focus near and far objects on the retina.

questions.q: What is the least distance of distinct vision for a normal eye?
questions.a: About 25 cm - objects nearer than this look blurred.

questions.q: Why can an elderly person not read small print clearly?
questions.a: With age the lens stiffens and ciliary muscles weaken, so near objects cannot be focused - presbyopia.

What is presbyopia and how is it corrected?
questions.a: Loss of the eye's power of accommodation with age; it is corrected using bifocal lenses (upper concave, lower convex).

Why does cataract blur vision and what is its remedy?
questions.a: The eye lens turns milky and opaque; surgery removes the cloudy lens and an artificial lens restores vision.

concepts.title: Refraction of Light through a Prism

solution_steps.name: sum_angles
solution_steps.explain: add the incidence and emergence angles at the two faces

solution_steps.name: half_bend
solution_steps.explain: average bending at the two faces

questions.q: Light passes through a prism of angle 60 deg with angle of incidence 40 deg and emergence 40 deg. Find the angle of deviation.
In a 60 deg prism, i = 45 deg and e = 45 deg. Calculate the deviation.
A ray enters a 60 deg prism at 50 deg and leaves at 40 deg. What is the angle of deviation?
For a prism with A = 60 deg, i = 55 deg and e = 45 deg, compute the deviation.
A thin prism of angle 50 deg is traversed by a ray with i = 30 deg and e = 50 deg. Find the deviation.
What is dispersion of light?
questions.a: Splitting of white light into its seven constituent colours because each colour bends by a different amount in a prism.

questions.q: Which colour bends most and which least while passing through a prism?
questions.a: Violet bends the most and red the least.

questions.q: Why does the sky look blue?
questions.a: Air molecules scatter short-wavelength blue light much more strongly than red, so scattered blue reaches our eyes.

questions.q: What is atmospheric refraction?
questions.a: Bending of light passing through layers of air of changing density, which shifts the apparent position of stars.

questions.q: Why does the sun appear to rise about two minutes before actual sunrise?
questions.a: Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight so we see the sun's image even when it is still below the horizon.

questions.q: Why do stars twinkle but planets do not?
questions.a: Starlight refracts through shifting air layers, changing brightness; planets are close enough to appear as steady extended sources.

concepts.title: Scattering of Light and Tyndall Effect

questions.q: What is the Tyndall effect?
questions.a: Scattering of a light beam by colloidal particles, making the beam's path visible, as sunlight in a misty forest.

questions.q: Why do clouds look white or sometimes red at sunset?
questions.a: Large droplets scatter all colours alike (white); at sunset light travels through more air, red dominates after scattering.

questions.q: What colour would the sky appear without any atmosphere?
questions.a: Black - with no air there is no scattering of sunlight towards the eye.
